name: Bachelor of Commerce (Applied)
description:
Box Hill Institute's Bachelor of Commerce (Applied) splits its three years into 12 core subjects (72 points), 8 major subjects (48 points), and 4 electives (24 points): accounting, finance, management, marketing, business ethics, and law all sit in the core before students specialise.

As a dual-sector provider, Box Hill teaches this degree the way it teaches its TAFE diplomas: smaller cohorts than a large university commerce school, and a direct line into the institute's own vocational accounting and business programs for students who want to start at certificate or diploma level and build up rather than enrolling in a bachelor's straight away.

The degree carries accreditation from both CPA Australia and Chartered Accountants Australia and New Zealand, which matters more than it might for a similarly-titled degree elsewhere. Box Hill isn't a research university trading on reputation, so professional body accreditation is the credential that does the work of assuring employers the accounting training meets the same bar as a larger institution's.
curriculum:
Year 1 — Foundations of Accounting; Economics for Business; Business Law; Marketing Principles; 2 further core subjects.
Year 2 — Financial Accounting; Management Accounting; Taxation Law; Corporations Law; 2 further core subjects; major subjects begin.
Year 3 — Auditing and Assurance; Strategic Management; Contemporary Issues in Accounting; remaining major subjects; 4 electives across the degree.
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (Australian Senior Secondary Certificate) or equivalent (approximate, typical bar)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 overall (Box Hill's own published bachelor-entry bar)

name: Bachelor of Computer Systems (Networking)
description:
This degree runs 19 core units plus 5 electives drawn from a choice of majors (cyber security, networking, or cloud and virtualisation), with the Networking major itself sitting inside a broader Computer Systems degree rather than being sold as a standalone qualification.

First year is deliberately generalist: basic networking, cloud computing, and introductory programming, so students don't have to commit hard to networking specifically before they've seen the alternatives. Second year gets specific fast: operating systems, cyber security, network security, systems security, virtualisation, and programming for web applications, alongside business and communication units that a purely technical program often skips. Third year moves into emerging ICT technologies, advanced security or virtualisation techniques, and entrepreneurship and innovation.

Box Hill delivers this in partnership with Cisco, VMware, and Microsoft, which shows up in the practical, vendor-relevant skills the networking major targets. Those skills sit closer to what a network administrator or systems engineer does day to day than a purely theoretical computer science curriculum, and they're useful for students aiming at Cisco or Microsoft certifications alongside the degree itself.
curriculum:
Year 1 — Introduction to Networking; Cloud Computing Fundamentals; Introductory Programming; IT Systems Fundamentals; foundational core units.
Year 2 — Operating Systems; Cyber Security Fundamentals; Network Security; Systems Security; Virtualisation; Programming for Web Applications; Business and Communication Skills.
Year 3 — Emerging ICT Technologies; Advanced Networking/Virtualisation Techniques; Entrepreneurship and Innovation; 5 electives (networking, cyber security, or cloud/virtualisation stream).

name: Bachelor of Early Childhood Education
description:
Box Hill's Bachelor of Early Childhood Education is built for people already working while they study, the program runs as blended delivery with classes on evenings and occasional Saturdays, and each core subject pairs 30 hours of face-to-face lecture, tutorial, and workshop time with around 5 hours of online activity rather than a standard daytime timetable.

The degree comprises 28 core subjects and 4 practicum subjects, totalling 80 days of supervised placement across a range of early childhood settings, deliberately including services other than the student's own workplace, so students already working in childcare still have to demonstrate their skills somewhere unfamiliar rather than only in a setting where staff already know them.

The program is recognised by the Australian Children's Education and Care Quality Authority and meets Victorian Institute of Teaching standards for Early Childhood Teacher registration, meaning graduates come out eligible to register as qualified early childhood teachers, not just educators, in Victoria.
curriculum:
Year 1 — Child Development; Foundations of Early Childhood Pedagogy; Health, Safety and Wellbeing in Early Childhood Settings; Practicum 1.
Year 2 — Curriculum Design for Early Learning; Language and Literacy Development; Working with Families and Communities; Practicum 2.
Year 3 — Leadership in Early Childhood Settings; Inclusive Practice and Additional Needs; Professional Practice and Ethics; Practicum 3.
Year 4 — Research and Reflective Practice in Early Childhood Education; Transition to Teaching; Practicum 4 (final placement block).
english_requirements: IELTS 7.5 (no band below 7.0) or equivalent (teaching registration requirement)

name: Bachelor of Fashion
description:
Box Hill Institute has run fashion design and merchandising training out of its Box Hill campus for decades, well before it offered bachelor's degrees at all, and the Bachelor of Fashion sits on top of that vocational base rather than starting from scratch as a purely academic program. The broader fashion degree family here splits 12 core units, 10 major units, and 6 electives across three years: pattern-making, garment construction, and textiles knowledge sit alongside business, marketing, and enterprise units rather than treating design as a purely creative pursuit separate from the commercial reality of running a label.

Students work with industry-standard equipment and, depending on the trimester, contribute to Box Hill's own fashion parades and graduate showcases, a public, portfolio-building event that functions as an informal industry pitch rather than a purely internal assessment.

Career paths lean toward fashion design, garment technology, buying and merchandising, and small-label entrepreneurship, reflecting Box Hill's applied, business-aware take on fashion education rather than a purely runway-focused design school model.
curriculum:
Year 1 — Fashion Design Fundamentals; Pattern-Making and Garment Construction 1; Textiles and Materials; Introduction to the Fashion Industry; core business unit.
Year 2 — Pattern-Making and Garment Construction 2; Fashion Illustration and Communication; Fashion Marketing; Sustainable Fashion Practice; major units begin.
Year 3 — Fashion Enterprise and Business Planning; Collection Development (culminating in graduate showcase); remaining major and elective units.
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion or equivalent; portfolio may be required

name: Bachelor of Hospitality Management
description:
The Bachelor of Hospitality Management at Box Hill covers accounting, marketing, business and hospitality law, workplace communications, strategic project management, and human resources management: a management-focused degree built for people planning to run hospitality operations rather than work the front line of them, though Box Hill's parallel commercial cookery and hospitality certificate programs mean many students arrive with genuine kitchen or floor experience already.

Small class sizes and direct lecturer contact are emphasised more than at a typical large university business school, consistent with Box Hill's TAFE-scale delivery model even at bachelor's level. A work-based hospitality management project gives students a real venue or business problem to solve rather than a hypothetical case study, drawing on Box Hill's existing industry relationships across Melbourne's hospitality sector.

Career paths include hotel and venue management, event management, hospitality operations, and food and beverage management, with the strategic project management and contemporary issues coursework aimed at people expected to run a shift, a venue, or eventually a business rather than simply staff one.
curriculum:
Year 1 — Introduction to Hospitality Management; Accounting for Hospitality; Workplace Communications; Marketing Principles.
Year 2 — Business and Hospitality Law; Human Resource Management; Contemporary Issues in Hospitality; Financial Management.
Year 3 — Strategic Project Management; Work-Based Hospitality Management Project; electives.

name: Bachelor of Information Technology
description:
Box Hill's Bachelor of Information Technology follows the same 12 core / 8 major / 4 elective structure as several of its other applied degrees, with specialisation streams in cyber security, data analytics and AI, cloud computing and IoT, and software engineering. It's TEQSA-accredited and pitched at AQF Level 7, the standard bachelor's level, despite Box Hill's identity as a TAFE first and university-level provider second.

That dual-sector status is arguably the more interesting fact about the degree: students can move between Box Hill's certificate and diploma-level IT courses and this bachelor's with credit transfer arrangements that a stand-alone university IT school doesn't usually offer as smoothly, useful for students who started in vocational IT training and want to step up without repeating content.

Career paths include software developer, cyber security analyst, data analyst, cloud engineer, and IT support/systems roles, with the elective structure letting students weight the final year toward whichever of the four specialisation areas matches where they want to work.
curriculum:
Year 1 — Introduction to Programming; IT Systems Fundamentals; Networking Basics; Database Fundamentals; core units.
Year 2 — Software Development; Cyber Security Principles; Cloud Computing Fundamentals; Data Analytics Foundations; major units begin.
Year 3 — Advanced specialisation units (cyber security, data analytics and AI, cloud and IoT, or software engineering); capstone IT project; 4 electives.

name: Bachelor of Music Industry (Major in Performance)
description:
Box Hill structures its Bachelor of Music Industry around six possible majors (Performance is one, alongside options like Audio Production and Composition), with a combined common core running through the first two years covering the music industry from multiple angles: innovation, creativity, entrepreneurship, and preparing for where the industry is heading rather than where it's been.

Once the major is chosen, it accounts for roughly half the remaining coursework, and students fill the rest by picking from a pool of more than sixty subjects, adding either two minors, a minor plus electives, or straight electives, a genuinely open structure compared to a fixed-major conservatoire degree. Full-time study runs at 16 contact hours a week plus an expected 16 hours of personal practice and study time, delivered face to face on weekdays.

Box Hill also builds in formal exit points most bachelor's degrees don't offer: a Diploma in Music Industry after one year and an Associate Degree in Music Industry after two, useful for students who want a credential if their circumstances change partway through, or who are testing whether a full three-year commitment is right for them.
curriculum:
Year 1 — Music Industry Foundations (common core); Performance Major 1; Innovation and Creativity in Music; electives.
Year 2 — Music Industry Perspectives (common core); Performance Major 2; entrepreneurship unit; electives or minor units. (Diploma exit available after Year 1; Associate Degree exit available after Year 2.)
Year 3 — Performance Major 3 (advanced); electives from the 60+ subject pool; capstone performance project.
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion or equivalent; audition required
